title: A cloud received him — the Son of Adam taken up and returning on the clouds
note: Enoch 1:9 re-quoted in full from the live verse; closing sentence mended to the live wording (holy ones).
summary_md: *A cloud received him out of their sight* (Acts 1:9), and two men in white promise *this same Yahusha (Jesus) … shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go* (Acts 1:11). The cloud is the Formed-one's own chariot. Daniel saw the same figure on the same clouds — *one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven* (Daniel 7:13) — the kaph honoring the incarnation: he resembled mortal-man because he took on flesh, while remaining the cloud-rider brought before the Ancient of days to receive the everlasting kingdom. The Revelation names the manner of the return: *behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him* (Revelation 1:7). And Zechariah names the place: they watched him go from the mount of Olives (Acts 1:12), and *his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives* (Zechariah 14:4) — he ascended from Olivet and to Olivet he returns. The Hebrew library already named the coming the angels promise: *And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, And of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.* (1 Enoch 1:9) — the same coming Jude quoted. The One taken up in a cloud returns on the clouds, and the holy ones who come with him are the seed of promise, gathered to him.

title: All power given — the Son of Adam seated on the throne of glory in 1 Enoch's Parables
note: Degraded prose rewritten from scratch; 51:1-2, 61:8, 62:2 and 62:9 quoted in full from the live text (62:6 dropped — the live verse is a different thought); Daniel 7:14 and Psalm 110:1 added from the index.
summary_md: When the risen King says *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18), he is not announcing something new. He is stepping into a seat the prophets had already described. Daniel saw it given: *And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.* (Daniel 7:14), and David heard the Father speak it: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit you at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.* (Psalms 110:1). The Parables of Enoch had set the same figure on the same throne long before: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed.* (1 Enoch 61:8), and again, *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). The power is over earth as much as heaven, because the kings of the earth answer to it: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9). And the first thing that authority does is open the graves and sort who comes out of them: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes. And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.* (1 Enoch 51:1-2). The empty tomb at the start of Matthew 28 and the *all power* at the end of it belong to the same morning. The Son of Adam who came out of the grave is the one who will call the rest of the seed out of theirs.

title: The Animal Apocalypse — the dispersed sheep gathered home
note: Was citation-only with two unmarked quotes; 89:74-75, 90:6 and 90:33 now quoted in full from the live text, hyphen-chain prose replaced; Matthew 4:19 kept, John 10:16 and Ezekiel 37:21 added from the index.
summary_md: *And he says unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.* (Matthew 4:19). The men he calls are being sent after sheep, and the Animal Apocalypse had already told the story of those sheep from the scattering to the gathering. First the blindness and the losing of them: *And as touching all this the eyes of those sheep were blinded so that they saw not, and (the eyes of) their shepherds likewise; and they delivered them in large numbers to their shepherds for destruction, and they trampled the sheep with their feet and devoured them. And Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep remained unmoved till all the sheep were dispersed over the field and mingled with them (i.e. the beasts), and they (i.e. the shepherds) did not save them out of the hand of the beasts.* (1 Enoch 89:74-75). Then, late in the age, a generation among them begins to see: *But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:6). And at the close, the ones who had been lost come home: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). That is the gathering Ezekiel promised, *Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* (Ezekiel 37:21), and it is the work the Shepherd names as his own: *And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.* (John 10:16). The disciples called by the lake are the first hands put to that gathering. The sheep who were mingled with the beasts open their eyes when the Shepherd's voice reaches them, and the fishers of men are sent to carry it.

title: Borne up on the wings — heaven, earth, abyss, the whole world shown
note: The old Enoch quote (whirlwind and chariot of fire) is 2 Kings 2:11 wording, not Enoch; replaced with the live 14:8 ascent and 19:3; Apocalypse of Abraham 12:9 and Ezekiel/Genesis kept as they stood.
summary_md: The angel takes the turtledove and pigeon for himself: *I will ascend upon the wings of the bird, in order to shew thee in heaven, and on the earth, and in the sea, and in the abyss, and in the under-world, and in the Garden of Eden, and in its rivers and in the fulness of the whole world and its circle — thou shalt gaze in them all* (Apocalypse of Abraham 12:9). Enoch had been carried the same way before him, not by his own strength but by the winds that were sent for him: *And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven.* (1 Enoch 14:8). And what he was shown was the whole of it, the ends of everything: *And I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things: and no man shall see as I have seen.* (1 Enoch 19:3). The opened heaven is the same fire Ezekiel saw come out of the north — *a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber* (Ezekiel 1:4) — and what Abraham will gaze upon is the whole creation, from the beginning: *In the beginning Elohim (God) created the heaven and the earth* (Genesis 1:1). The same hand that lifted Enoch lifts Abraham, and shows him the same world.

title: Forty days, no bread, no water — the fast of the mountain
note: Invented 14:2 quote replaced with the live 19:3 (the thought it was reaching for); canon quotes kept as they stood.
summary_md: Abraham journeys to the holy mount as Moses fasted before the LORD: *And we went, the two of us together, forty days and nights, and I ate no bread, and drank no water, because my food was to see the angel who was with me, and his speech — that was my drink* (Apocalypse of Abraham 12:1). This is the very measure of the mountain-fast: *And he was there with Yahuah (LORD) forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water* (Exodus 34:28), and again *then I abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, I neither did eat bread nor drink water* (Deuteronomy 9:9). What sustained Abraham was what he was shown, and Enoch says the same of his own seeing, that it was given to him alone and to no other man: *And I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things: and no man shall see as I have seen.* (1 Enoch 19:3). The friend of Elohim is fed not by bread but by the word of the messenger, and the sight he is given on the mountain is his meat.

title: Borne up with many winds to the flaming fire — the chariot ascent
note: Invented 14:3 quote replaced with the live 14:8-9 (winds bearing Enoch up to the wall of fire); Ezekiel kept.
summary_md: *And he bore me to the borders of the flaming fire, and we ascended as with many winds to the heaven which was fixed upon the surface* (Apocalypse of Abraham 15:4). The road Abraham is carried on is the road Enoch was carried on first, winds doing the lifting and fire waiting at the top of the climb: *And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven. And I went in till I drew nigh to a wall which is built of crystals and surrounded by tongues of fire: and it began to affright me.* (1 Enoch 14:8-9). Ezekiel's throne-vision comes wrapped in the same wind and the same fire: *And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it... out of the midst of the fire* (Ezekiel 1:4). Three men, one ascent, and the same fiery threshold at the border of the heavens.

title: The chariot of fiery wheels full of eyes
note: Invented 14:3 chariot quote replaced with the live 14:18-19 (the throne with wheels and the fire beneath it); Ezekiel and Daniel kept.
summary_md: Behind the living creatures Abraham sees *a chariot with fiery wheels, each wheel full of eyes round about; and over the wheels was a throne... covered with fire* (Apocalypse of Abraham 18:9). Ezekiel's merkabah is this very wheelwork — *their rings were full of eyes round about them four* (Ezekiel 1:18), the wheel within the wheel — *and their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about, even the wheels that they four had* (Ezekiel 10:12). Daniel saw the Ancient of days on the same flaming wheels — *his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire* (Daniel 7:9). And Enoch, brought into the second house, saw the throne before any of them: *And I looked and saw therein a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim. And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon.* (1 Enoch 14:18-19). The wheels, the cherubim, the fire pouring out from under the seat: every seer who is taken up is shown the same chariot, because there is only one throne.

title: The Beatitudes — the blessing pronounced over the righteous and elect
note: Citation-only gloss in hyphen-chain prose; rewritten with 1:8, 5:7 and 58:2-3 quoted in full from the live text, Matthew 5:3, 5:4, 5:10 and Wisdom 3:1, 3:9 added from the index.
summary_md: *Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:3). *Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.* (Matthew 5:4). *Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:10). The pulpit has long read these as a ladder, conditions a person meets in order to get in. Enoch had already pronounced the same blessing, and he pronounced it over a people, not over a performance: *But with the righteous He will make peace. And will protect the elect, And mercy shall be upon them. And they shall all belong to Elohim (God), And they shall be prospered, And they shall all be blessed. And He will help them all, And light shall appear unto them, And He will make peace with them.* (1 Enoch 1:8). The comfort promised to the mourners is this light and this peace, and the inheritance is the same one the meek are told they will receive: *And for you the godless there shall be a curse. But for the elect there shall be light and joy and peace, And they shall inherit the earth.* (1 Enoch 5:7). Then the form itself, blessed-are-ye, spoken to the persecuted: *Blessed are ye, ye righteous and elect, For glorious shall be your lot. And the righteous shall be in the light of the sun, And the elect in the light of eternal life: The days of their life shall be unending, And the days of the holy without number.* (1 Enoch 58:2-3). The Wisdom of Solomon says it the same way, that *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (the Wisdom of Solomon 3:1), and that *grace and mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect* (the Wisdom of Solomon 3:9). Read beside these, the Beatitudes describe the citizens the King has come to gather. The blessing is on them because of who they are to him, and the poverty of spirit, the mourning, the hunger for righteousness are what that people looks like in the lands of their scattering before he brings them home.

title: The binding of the Watchers — Azazel bound hand and foot, and the strong man bound
note: Degraded prose rewritten; 10:4-6, 54:5 and Jubilees 10:11 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew 12:28-29 and Revelation 20:2-3 from the index. The old 'inaugurated binding now' framing dropped; the binding of the adversary is set at the end where Revelation puts it.
summary_md: *But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of Elohim (God), then the kingdom of Elohim (God) is come unto you. Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.* (Matthew 12:28-29). The picture of a strong one bound so that his house can be plundered was not drawn fresh for the Pharisees. It is how the Watchers were dealt with, and the library had told it in detail: *And again Yahuah (Lord) said to Raphael: ‘Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness: and make an opening in the desert, which is in Dûdâêl, and cast him therein. And place upon him rough and jagged rocks, and cover him with darkness, and let him abide there for ever, and cover his face that he may not see light. And on the day of the great judgement he shall be cast into the fire.* (1 Enoch 10:4-6). The chains were not for him alone: *And he said unto me: ‘These are being prepared for the hosts of Azâzêl, so that they may take them and cast them into the abyss of complete condemnation, and they shall cover their jaws with rough stones as Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits commanded.* (1 Enoch 54:5). Jubilees tells why there are still spirits to cast out at all: *And we did according to all His words: all the malignant evil ones we bound in the place of condemnation, and a tenth part of them we left that they might be subject before Satan on the earth.* (Jubilees 10:11). The devils Yahusha (Jesus) drives out are that tenth, the loose remainder of a host already mostly in chains, and the one they serve is the strong man whose binding is still ahead: *And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.* (Revelation 20:2-3). When the King empties a man of a devil by the Spirit, the house is being spoiled by the one who has the authority to bind its master. That is why he could say the kingdom had come upon them.

title: Bound and cast into the furnace of fire — the Watchers' judgement and the tares
note: Degraded prose rewritten; 10:12-13, 54:6 and 90:24-25 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew 13:41-42 from the index; internal thread references removed.
summary_md: *The Son of Adam shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity; And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 13:41-42). The tares are gathered first and bound in bundles to burn, and the reapers are angels. Enoch had watched the same angels do the same work on the Watchers: *And when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated. In those days they shall be led off to the abyss of fire: and to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever.* (1 Enoch 10:12-13). The Parables name the hands that carry them there and the day it happens: *And Michael, and Gabriel, and Raphael, and Phanuel shall take hold of them on that great day, and cast them on that day into the burning furnace, that Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits may take vengeance on them for their unrighteousness in becoming subject to Satan and leading astray those who dwell on the earth.’* (1 Enoch 54:6). And the Animal Apocalypse shows the order of it at the end, the fallen stars first and then the shepherds who destroyed the sheep: *And the judgement was held first over the stars, and they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and they were cast into an abyss, full of fire and flaming, and full of pillars of fire. And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:24-25). The burning furnace of the parable is this abyss. The angels who bound Azazel in the desert are the angels sent at the harvest, and what they gather out of the kingdom goes where the Watchers went. The seed sown by the enemy is dealt with the same way the enemy's own hosts were dealt with, and before the wheat is brought in.

title: The fowls that devour the seed — Mastema's birds and the spirits of the Watchers
note: Degraded prose rewritten; 1 Enoch 19:1 quoted in full from the live text; Jubilees 11:11 and the Matthew quotes kept as they stood; Matthew 13:19 completed from the index.
summary_md: In the parable the seed by the wayside is lost when *fowls came and devoured them up* (Matthew 13:4), and the King does not leave the birds as scenery. He tells us who they are: *When any one hears the word of the kingdom, and understands it not, then comes the wicked one, and catches away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.* (Matthew 13:19). Jubilees had already put birds in the adversary's hand, sent against the seed in the days of Abraham's father: *Prince Mastema sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land, in order to destroy the land, so as to rob the children of men of their labours. Before they could plough in the seed, the ravens picked it from the surface of the ground* (Jubilees 11:11). And Enoch names the spirits that do the robbing, where they came from and what they are working toward: *And Uriel said to me: ‘Here shall stand the angels who have connected themselves with women, and their spirits assuming many different forms are defiling mankind and shall lead them astray into sacrificing to demons as gods, (here shall they stand,) till the day of the great judgement in which they shall be judged till they are made an end of.* (1 Enoch 19:1). Abraham drove the fowls off his sacrifice (Genesis 15:11); Mastema sent them against the furrows; the wicked one sends them against the heart where the word of the kingdom has just been sown. It is one enemy with one aim, to take the seed before it can root, and the same birds come back later in the chapter to lodge in the branches of the mustard tree, because what grows in the field grows with the enemy still working in it until the harvest.

title: The righteous stands in boldness before those who condemned him — Wisdom 5 and 1 Enoch 95
note: Degraded prose rewritten; 1 Enoch 95:6-7 quoted in full from the live text; Wisdom 5 quotes kept, Matthew 12:14 and Wisdom 5:4-5 completed from the index.
summary_md: *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). A council of the religious sits to condemn a righteous man, and the verdict it reaches stands for a season. The Wisdom of Solomon had already written the day that verdict is turned over: *then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him* (the Wisdom of Solomon 5:1), and the men who condemned him are made to say out loud what they got wrong: *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (the Wisdom of Solomon 5:4-5). Enoch pronounces the woe on that council and on every one like it, and says the sentence will fall on them in the same coin: *Woe to you, lying witnesses, And to those who weigh out injustice, For suddenly shall ye perish. Woe to you, sinners, for ye persecute the righteous; For ye shall be delivered up and persecuted because of injustice, And heavy shall its yoke be upon you.* (1 Enoch 95:6-7). The road from questioning his disciples over dinner, to calling him a glutton and a friend of sinners, to plotting his death, is the road the lying witnesses walk, and it ends at the cross. But the resurrection is the first turning of the verdict, and the day of judgement is the last. The same thing happens to the seed who keep his commandments today, condemned by councils that hold the pulpit, and the same reversal is waiting for them.

title: A man's foes shall be they of his own household — the family torn in the day of destruction
note: Degraded prose rewritten; 1 Enoch 99:5 and 100:1-2 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew 10:34-36 from the index.
summary_md: *Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.* (Matthew 10:34-36). He is quoting Micah, and Micah is describing a day. Enoch describes the same day, and the house is where it tears first: *And in those days the destitute shall go forth and carry off their children, And they shall abandon them, so that their children shall perish through them: Yea, they shall abandon their children (that are still) sucklings, and not return to them, And shall have no pity on their beloved ones.* (1 Enoch 99:5). Then the blood: *And in those days in one place the fathers together with their sons shall be smitten And brothers one with another shall fall in death Till the streams flow with their blood. For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons’ sons, And the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: From dawn till sunset they shall slay one another.* (1 Enoch 100:1-2). The enmity set in the garden between the two seeds does not stop at the front door. Wheat and tares can be born under one roof, and when the Shepherd's voice is heard by one and not the other, the line runs straight through the family. What the King warns his disciples of in this age is the first showing of the division Enoch saw finished in the day of destruction, when the house that would not hear falls on itself.

title: This is the Son of Adam — the voice that names him at the investiture
note: The '39:5 voice of the Holy One' quote is not in the live text and was dropped; the 'This is the Son of Adam' words live at 71:14, not 62:7 — re-cited and quoted in full with 62:7; Matthew 3:17 and Ascension 11:32 from the index.
summary_md: *And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.* (Matthew 3:17). A voice from above the water names the one standing in it. Enoch heard the same form of words spoken over the same figure when he was carried up into the heavens: *And he (i.e. the angel) came to me and greeted me with His voice, and said unto me: ‘This is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness, And righteousness abides over him, And the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.’* (1 Enoch 71:14). This is the Son of Adam, this is my beloved Son. The naming at the Jordan is public, and the Parables explain why it had to come as a disclosure and not as common knowledge: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). The one hidden with the Father from the beginning is revealed to the elect, and at the river the revealing is spoken out loud. The Ascension of Isaiah carries the other end of the arc, the Beloved who came down in the form of a man going back up: *And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:32). Descent, naming, ascent. The voice at the Jordan is one point on a line the library had already drawn end to end.

title: Gather all the tribes of Jacob — Sirach 36 and the return to the house in 1 Enoch 90
note: Degraded prose rewritten; the invented 90:18 quote replaced by 90:33 quoted in full; Sirach quotes kept as they stood; Isaiah 43:5-6 added from the index.
summary_md: *And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 8:11). East and west is the language of the gathering, and the prophets used it of a seed, not of strangers: *Fear not: for I am with you: I will bring your seed from the east, and gather you from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth;* (Isaiah 43:5-6). Sirach prays for exactly this, and names who is being gathered: *gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11), and the people whose name the prayer rests on, *Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn* (Ecclesiasticus 36:12). Enoch saw the end of that prayer in the Animal Apocalypse, the scattered sheep brought back into the house: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). The many from east and west who sit at the table with the patriarchs are the tribes of Jacob come home, the sons and daughters brought from far. The children of the kingdom cast out in the next verse are not Judah set aside for a church; they are the unfruitful of the house, sifted under the rod as Ezekiel 20 says the whole gathered people will be. The seat at the table is for the seed that hears, wherever the scattering carried it.

title: The heavens opened at the investiture — the open door of the throne-room
note: Citation-only; 14:15 and 71:1 now quoted in full from the live text, Testament of Levi quote kept, Matthew 3:16 from the index.
summary_md: *And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:* (Matthew 3:16). Heaven opens over a man at the moment he is set apart for service. Levi was shown it at his own calling to the priesthood: *behold the heavens were opened, and an angel of Elohim (God) said to me, Levi, enter* (Testament of Levi 2:6). Enoch was shown what the open heaven opens onto. First the door itself: *And I beheld a vision, And lo! there was a second house, greater than the former, and the entire portal stood open before me, and it was built of flames of fire.* (1 Enoch 14:15). Then, in the Parables, the ascent into that house where the Son of Adam is named: *And it came to pass after this that my spirit was translated And it ascended into the heavens: And I saw the holy sons of Elohim (God). They were stepping on flames of fire: Their garments were white [and their raiment], And their faces shone like snow.* (1 Enoch 71:1). The portal that stood open before Enoch is the heaven that opened over the Jordan. What came down through it onto the Son was the Spirit, and what was spoken through it was the Father's voice. The priesthood Levi entered through an open heaven and the office the Son is sealed into at the water are reached through the same door.

title: When he saw his glory — the enthroned One Isaiah saw is the Formed Son
note: The mechanical re-quote had landed on 18:8-9 (a mountain 'like the throne'); the throne-vision the summary is about is 14:18-20, quoted in full instead.
summary_md: Isaiah saw a Person on the throne: *In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also Yahuah (Lord) sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple* (Isaiah 6:1); *for mine eyes have seen the King, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (6:5). John reads this very chapter and names whose glory it was. He first quotes the commission of 6:10 — *He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them* (John 12:40) — and then declares: *These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him* (John 12:41). The glory that filled the temple was HIS glory. This is the Formed and the Formless: the visible enthroned Glory whom Isaiah saw is the Formed Son, the expressed Word drawn from the Formless Father — the One who appeared, who is Yahuah, and who HAS a Father. Not co-equal trinitarian persons; not a modalist collapse — the One enthroned, of whom Isaiah *spake*, is Yahusha (Jesus). Enoch was brought before the same throne and could say no more of the One on it than Isaiah could: *And I looked and saw therein a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim. And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon. And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow.* (1 Enoch 14:18-20) — the throne high and lifted up, the fire, the Glory none could look upon.

title: Behold, I create new heavens and a new earth — the keystone of the new creation
note: Invented 45:4 quote replaced with the live 45:4-5 in full; the rest stands.
summary_md: Here is the keystone toward which the whole promise runs: *For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind* (Isaiah 65:17). Peter names this very promise as the hope of the people: *Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness* (2 Peter 3:13). John sees it come: *And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea* (Revelation 21:1) — and *the former things are passed away* (Revelation 21:4), the very *former* that *shall not be remembered, nor come into mind*. Isaiah himself seals its permanence in the next chapter: *For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith Yahuah (LORD), so shall your seed and your name remain* (Isaiah 66:22) — the new creation endures, and the seed of promise and the name endure with it. The Parables of Enoch sing the same renewal, and they put the Elect One in the middle of it: *Then will I cause Mine Elect One to dwell among them. And I will transform the heaven and make it an eternal blessing and light: And I will transform the earth and make it a blessing: And I will cause Mine elect ones to dwell upon it: But the sinners and evil-doers shall not set foot thereon.* (1 Enoch 45:4-5). The Father is the formless Source; the Elect One dwelling among his people is the Formed Son. The creating of Isaiah, the looking-for of Peter, the seeing of John, the transforming of the Parables — one new creation, the end every promise was pointed at.

title: By fire and by his sword will Yahuah plead with all flesh — the fiery judgment and the rebels' end
note: 1:9 re-quoted in full from the live verse (holy ones); the invented 45:5 'straw in the fire' quote replaced with the live 45:5-6.
summary_md: Against the rejoicing of the restored comes the fire upon the rebels: *For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will Yahuah (LORD) plead with all flesh: and the slain of Yahuah (LORD) shall be many* (Isaiah 66:15-16). The Formed Son is the executor of this fire: *when the Lord Yahusha (Lord Jesus) shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels* (2 Thessalonians 1:7), *In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not Elohim (God)* (1:8); *out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations... and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of El Shaddai (Almighty God)* (Revelation 19:15). The day burns as an oven: *all that do wickedly, shall be stubble; and the day that cometh shall burn them up* (Malachi 4:1); the heavens are *reserved unto fire against the day of judgment* (2 Peter 3:7). Enoch opens his whole book on this advent, the verse Jude quotes by name: *And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, And of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.* (1 Enoch 1:9). And the Parables say where the sinners stand when the earth is made new, which is nowhere on it: *And I will transform the earth and make it a blessing: And I will cause Mine elect ones to dwell upon it: But the sinners and evil-doers shall not set foot thereon. For I have provided and satisfied with peace My righteous ones And have caused them to dwell before Me: But for the sinners there is judgement impending with Me, So that I shall destroy them from the face of the earth.* (1 Enoch 45:5-6). The book's very last verse fixes the rebels' final state, quoted verbatim by Yahusha of Gehenna: *they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched* (66:24); *Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched* (Mark 9:48); *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake... some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2). The swine's-flesh rebels of v.17 are the *all flesh* this fire pleads against — the dietary rebellion judged, not licensed.

title: From one sabbath to another shall all flesh come to worship — the appointed times into eternity
note: Invented 45:4 fragment replaced with the live 45:4-5 in full; the rest stands.
summary_md: The book closes on the plainest answer to lawlessness in the whole Tanakh: *For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith Yahuah (LORD), so shall your seed and your name remain. And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 66:22-23). The new moons AND the sabbaths are KEPT BY ALL FLESH in the new creation — the appointed times are not abolished; they continue into eternity, as permanent as the new heavens themselves, and the seed and name of the people remain with them. The new creation is the one just promised: *behold, I create new heavens and a new earth* (Isaiah 65:17); *I saw a new heaven and a new earth* (Revelation 21:1); *new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness* (2 Peter 3:13); and Enoch's Parables, where the Elect One dwells among the elect on the earth made new: *Then will I cause Mine Elect One to dwell among them. And I will transform the heaven and make it an eternal blessing and light: And I will transform the earth and make it a blessing: And I will cause Mine elect ones to dwell upon it: But the sinners and evil-doers shall not set foot thereon.* (1 Enoch 45:4-5). Zechariah names the same kept feast: *every one that is left of all the nations... shall... go up from year to year to worship the King... and to keep the feast of tabernacles* (Zechariah 14:16). And Colossians, so often misread as abolition, is the shadow whose BODY remains: *Let no man therefore judge you... of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Messiah (Christ)* (Colossians 2:16-17) — the shadow stands because the body stands; Paul forbids the outsider judging those who keep them, while Isaiah shows all flesh keeping them on into the new heavens. The filter holds: *hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments* (1 John 2:3). Any reading that abolishes the kept sabbath fails the test Isaiah's own ending sets, for the very last vision of the book is all flesh worshipping from sabbath to sabbath, for ever.

title: Enoch prophesied — the seventh from Adam and the day of judgment
note: No Enoch quote to grade; 'the live 1 Enoch' and 'one apparatus' phrasing replaced with plain words.
summary_md: Before he is taken, Jasher's Enoch gives a last charge: *And now therefore I will teach you wisdom and knowledge and will give you instruction before I leave you, how to act upon earth by which you may live* (Jasher 3:25), and *he placed before them statutes and judgments to do upon earth, and he made peace amongst them, and he taught them everlasting life* (Jasher 3:26). The Renewed Covenant remembers this Enoch as a prophet of the judgment to come: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints,* (Jude 1:14), *To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds* (Jude 1:15). The book of Enoch itself is the testimony Jude is quoting, the witness of the man who *placed the testimony on earth for all the children of men and for their generations* (Jubilees 4:19) and *should recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.* (Jubilees 4:24). The statutes he taught and the judgment he warned of come from the same mouth, and they belong together. It ain't new.

title: Enoch was not, for Elohim took him — translated that he should not see death
note: The 'chariot of fire' Enoch quote is 2 Kings 2:11 wording and is nowhere in Enoch; replaced with the live 39:3 and 14:8, which do describe his being carried off.
summary_md: Jasher's whole chapter drives to the moment Genesis states in five words. An angel calls again — *behold an angel of Yahuah (the Lord) then called to Enoch from heaven, and wished to bring him up to heaven to make him reign there over the sons of Elohim* (Jasher 3:23) — and *it was upon the seventh day that Enoch ascended into heaven in a whirlwind, with horses and chariots of fire.* (Jasher 3:36). That is Genesis told long: *And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him.* (Genesis 5:24). The Renewed Covenant reads it as faith: *By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because Elohim (God) had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased Elohim (God).* (Hebrews 11:5). Enoch tells the whirlwind in his own words: *And in those days a whirlwind carried me off from the earth, And set me down at the end of the heavens.* (1 Enoch 39:3), and how the winds bore him up: *And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven.* (1 Enoch 14:8). Jubilees seals the taking: *And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour* (Jubilees 4:23). The translation of Enoch is one event held by five witnesses, and not one of them has him die.

title: Yahuah shut him in — the men shut out, all flesh died
note: Mentions 1 Enoch only as a witness name beside Jasher 4 and Jubilees 5; nothing quoted, nothing to fix.
summary_md: Jasher records the shutting of the door and the perishing of all flesh: *And Noah and his household, and all the living creatures that were with him, came into the ark on account of the waters of the flood, and Yahuah (the Lord) shut him in* (Jasher 6:15), and *all flesh that was upon the earth or in the waters died, whether men, animals, beasts, creeping things or birds of the air, and there only remained Noah and those that were with him in the ark* (Jasher 6:26). Genesis is the same shutting and the same death: *and Yahuah (LORD) shut him in* (Genesis 7:16), and *And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground… and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark* (Genesis 7:23). Jasher adds the seven hundred thousand who begged at the door (Jasher 6:17) — the rebellion that said *that he does not exist* (Jasher 6:19) — but the verdict is the canon's: the door of mercy was shut after a hundred and twenty years of warning. The flood is judgment on the corrupted earth that the Watchers (Jasher 4, 1 Enoch, Jubilees 5) defiled.

title: Adam's garments, Enoch translated, and the birth of Abram
note: No Enoch quote; the 'live 1 Enoch and Jubilees apparatus' sentence replaced with plain words.
summary_md: Verse 18 carries two threads the chosen line will need. First the garments: *the garments of skin which Elohim made for Adam and his wife... were given to Enoch, the son of Jared, and when Enoch was taken up to Elohim, he gave them to Methuselah, his son* (Jasher 7:18). Enoch's being taken up is the canon's own — *And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him* (Genesis 5:24), which the witness names as translation by faith: *By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because Elohim (God) had translated him* (Hebrews 11:5). Jasher 3, the book of Enoch, and Jubilees all tell that same taking at length. Then the elect line surfaces against Nimrod's kingdom: *Terah was seventy years old when he begat him, and Terah called the name of his son that was born to him Abram* (Jasher 7:18). It ain't new: *And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran* (Genesis 11:26). And the canon remembers Terah served other gods — *even Terah, the father of Abraham... and they served other gods* (Joshua 24:2) — out of which the called seed Abram is taken: the wheat among the tares of Nimrod's Babel.

title: Exalted for a little while, but brought low
note: All three Enoch quotes were invented (96:10 does not exist); replaced with the live 96:1, 96:5-6 and 96:8 in full.
summary_md: Job ends the catalogue not with despair but with the verdict the retribution doctrine could not give him on its own terms: *He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no man is sure of life... They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn* (Job 24:22,24). The strong man's height is real, and brief. Asaph was staggered by the same prosperity — *envious... when I saw the prosperity of the wicked* (Psalm 73:3) — until the sanctuary opened his eyes: *Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou castedst them down into destruction* (Psalm 73:18); *as a dream when one awaketh; so, O Yahuah (Lord), when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image* (Psalm 73:20). Enoch says the same thing to the righteous first, before he turns to the mighty: *Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 96:1). Then the woes, and they read like Job's catalogue turned into a sentence: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might. Woe to you who drink water from every fountain, For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away, Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.* (1 Enoch 96:5-6), and *Woe to you, ye mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 96:8). Job's sickle, Asaph's waking dream, Enoch's withering. The exaltation is *a little while*; the cutting off is sure, and the day that ends the mighty is the day that begins the good days of the righteous.

title: Where Wast Thou When I Laid the Foundations — and the Morning Stars Sang
note: Invented 18:1-2 quote replaced with the live 18:1-3 in full; the rest stands.
summary_md: *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?... Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of Elohim (God) shouted for joy?* (Job 38:4-7). The man was not there; the Creator alone laid them — and He laid them with Wisdom, the Formed Son: *When he... appointed the foundations of the earth: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight* (Proverbs 8:29-30). The foundations stand fixed forever: *Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever* (Psalm 104:5). The NT names the agent through whom they were laid: *For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible... all things were created by him, and for him* (Colossians 1:16) — the Formed Son, who has a Father, never the Father Himself. The *sons of Elohim (God)* who *shouted for joy* are the same heavenly court that opens the book: *Now there was a day when the sons of Elohim (God) came to present themselves before Yahuah (LORD)* (Job 1:6). Job was not there, but Enoch was shown the place, foundations and corner-stone and all: *I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth. And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven. And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:1-3). The question put to Job out of the whirlwind has an answer in the library, and the answer is a man who was carried to see it.

title: The resurrection and the life — the earth giving back its dead in 2 Esdras and 1 Enoch
note: Mechanical re-quote of 51:1-2 holds; the closing prose still spoke of the Elect One 'arising', which is 51:5 — added in full so the prose has its verse; 'architecture' wording plained.
summary_md:
At the grave of Lazaros, Martha confesses the resurrection at the last day, and the Formed one answers with a name: *I am the resurrection, and the life.* The inherited reading treats the raising of Lazaros as a stand-alone miracle and the saying as a comfort. The Hebrew library shows what the saying stands on: the earth, Sheol, and death itself giving back the dead at the resurrection, and the Elect One arising to choose the righteous from among them.

*Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Yahusha (Jesus) said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.* (John 11:24-26)

*And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32)

*And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes. And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.* (1 Enoch 51:1-2)

*For in those days the Elect One shall arise, And the earth shall rejoice, And the righteous shall dwell upon it, And the elect shall walk thereon.* (1 Enoch 51:5)

Martha's hope — *the resurrection at the last day* — is the Hebrew library's own hope: the earth restoring the sleeping, the dust giving back those in silence, Sheol and death giving back what they hold. And the library binds that resurrection to a person, the Elect One who arises and chooses the righteous from among the raised. John 11:25 says the same thing in the first person. The Formed one is himself the resurrection the library awaited, the Elect One whose arising brings the dead back from the earth, from Sheol, from death's keeping. The raising of Lazaros — *Lazarus, come forth* — is the firstfruit sign of it, the head doing in one grave what the whole gathered body will follow him through at the last day.

title: The hour is come — the Son of Adam glorified and enthroned in the Enochic Parables
note: Mechanical re-quotes (71:14, 61:9) hold; prose mended so the naming is the angel's voice as 71:14 has it, 61:8 added in full for the enthronement, 'the framework hears / architecture' wording plained.
summary_md:
When the Greeks at the feast ask to see him, the Formed one answers not with an audience but with the hour: *the hour is come, that the Son of Adam should be glorified.* The inherited reading hears *glorified* as a soft word for the crucifixion. It carries more than that. The Son of Adam is a named figure in the Hebrew library, shown to Enoch beside the Head of Days and seated on the throne of glory, and his glorifying is the enthronement the Parables already wrote, reached by way of the lifting-up.

*And Yahusha (Jesus) answered them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of Adam should be glorified.* (John 12:23)

*Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.* (John 12:28)

*And he (i.e. the angel) came to me and greeted me with His voice, and said unto me: ‘This is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness, And righteousness abides over him, And the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.’* (1 Enoch 71:14)

*And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed. And when he shall lift up his countenance To judge their secret ways according to the word of the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And their path according to the way of the righteous judgement of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, Then shall they all with one voice speak and bless, And glorify and extol and sanctify the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 61:8-9)

The Son of Adam is not a veil over a generic human. The library names him — *this is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness* — and the righteousness of the Head of Days never forsakes him. In the Parables the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits is glorified at the moment the Elect One is set on the throne and lifts up his face to judge; John 12:28 puts the same thing in the Father's own voice from heaven: *Father, glorify thy name ... I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.* The hour of the Son of Adam's glorifying is the hour the Father's name is glorified. And the path to the throne the Parables describe runs through the lifting-up: *I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me* (John 12:32). The Son of Adam the library names beside the Head of Days is the Formed one whose hour has come, glorified through the cross and drawing the gathered home.

title: The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do (Deuteronomy 18; Daniel 7; 1 Enoch 49, 61, 71)
note: Invented 62:6-7 quote replaced: the seating is 61:8 and the naming is 71:14, both quoted in full from the live text; 49:2,4 abridged quote kept (stands).
summary_md:
Here is the heart of who the Son is. *The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise* (John 5:19). Not an independent deity acting on his own; not a creature improvising. The Formed Son does only what he sees the Father do.

Moses foretold him so: *I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren... and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.* (Deuteronomy 18:18). The Prophet carries the Sender's word, never his own. And the kingdom is *given*: *one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days* (Daniel 7:13) — the kaph preserved, the Formed Son brought near — *and there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom... his dominion is an everlasting dominion* (Daniel 7:14). Given by the Father, received by the Son. So *the Father hath given to the Son to have life in himself, and hath given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of Adam* (John 5:26-27).

The older witnesses say the same. *Because the Elect One standeth before Yahuah (God) of Spirits... he shall judge the secret things, And none shall be able to utter a lying word before him* (1 Enoch 49:2,4): the Son stands before the Father and judges by what he is given. The throne is given too: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed.* (1 Enoch 61:8). And his standing with the Father is what the angel names over him: *And he (i.e. the angel) came to me and greeted me with His voice, and said unto me: ‘This is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness, And righteousness abides over him, And the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.’* (1 Enoch 71:14). The Father seats the Son of Adam to judge, and the righteousness he judges by is the Head of Days' own. One will, one work: the Father shows, the Son does; the Father gives, the Son receives.

title: Sodom overthrown, Lot delivered — judgment engraved on the tables
note: 'the framework leans on' removed; 1 Enoch 10:14 quoted in full instead of cited bare.
summary_md: In the same month judgment falls: *And in this month Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day* (Jubilees 16:5). This is the Genesis overthrow retold — *Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven; And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain* (Genesis 19:24-25). Jubilees keeps the deliverance of Lot for Abraham's sake exactly as Genesis does: *But Lot we saved; for Elohim (God) remembered Abraham, and sent him out from the midst of the overthrow* (Jubilees 16:6) — word for word the Torah's *and it came to pass, when Elohim (God) destroyed the cities of the plain, that Elohim (God) remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow* (Genesis 19:29). But Jubilees adds something Genesis leaves unsaid, a verdict already on the heavenly tables: the uncleanness of Sodom is *commanded and engraven concerning all his seed, on the heavenly tables, to remove them and root them out* (Jubilees 16:9). The judgment of the wicked was written before it fell, and the sentence runs on through everyone who joins them, the way the Watchers' doom was fixed before their day came: *And whosoever shall be condemned and destroyed will from thenceforth be bound together with them to the end of all generations.* (1 Enoch 10:14).

title: The 364-day year on the heavenly tablets, and the sinners who follow the moon
note: The 'alter the times… eat blood' quote is nowhere in Enoch and was dropped; 74:12 and 82:4-6 quoted in full from the live text (the 364-day count and the men who go wrong in the reckoning); internal references removed.
summary_md: The calendar climax. Jubilees commands the solar reckoning engraved on the tablets — *And command you the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they observe the years according to this reckoning-three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts* (Jubilees 6:32) — and warns that those who watch the moon will wreck the appointed times: *For there will be those who will assuredly make observations of the moon–now (it) disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon* (Jubilees 6:36), confounding the holy with the unclean, *for they will go wrong as to the months and sabbaths and feasts and jubilees* (Jubilees 6:37). Enoch's book of the luminaries gives the same count and says it will not drift: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). And it names the same fault Jubilees names, men who leave the four added days out of the reckoning and so lose the year: *Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days. Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately. For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded (thereon) for ever, one in the first portal and one in the third, and one in the fourth and one in the sixth, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.* (1 Enoch 82:4-6). Daniel names the same spirit at work in the last days: *and think to change times and laws* (Daniel 7:25). The order is fixed on the heavenly tablets. To follow the moon's drift is to lose the path of the years, and with it the feasts the year was made to carry.

title: Shem's lot — the middle of the earth, Eden, Sinai and Zion the navel
note: 26:1 re-quoted in full from the live verse; 'the framework's land' and 'the live Enoch apparatus' phrasing removed.
summary_md: The first lot falls to Shem, and it is the holy centre: *And there came forth on the writing as Shem’s lot the middle of the earth which he should take as an inheritance for himself and for his sons for the generations of eternity* (Jubilees 8:11), *that they should possess it for ever to his generations for evermore* (Jubilees 8:17). And the reason is unveiled: *he knew that the Garden of Eden is the holy of holies, and the dwelling of Yahuah (God), and Mount Sinai the centre of the desert, and Mount Zion–the centre of the navel of the earth: these three were created as holy places facing each other* (Jubilees 8:18). This is the land of promise itself, with Jerusalem at the centre of the world. Ezekiel says it plainly: *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations and countries that are round about her* (Ezekiel 5:5), and again of the regathered people *that dwell in the midst of the land* (Ezekiel 38:12). Enoch was walked to the same centre on his journeys and saw the mountain standing in it: *And I went from thence to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed place in which there were trees with branches abiding and blooming [of a dismembered tree]. And there I saw a holy mountain, and underneath the mountain to the east there was a stream and it flowed towards the south.* (1 Enoch 26:1-2) — Zion, the navel, the kept inheritance of the seed.

title: The angels which kept not their first estate — the Watchers reserved in everlasting chains (Genesis 6; 1 Enoch 10, 13, 21; Jubilees 5; 1 Peter 3, 2 Peter 2)
note: Mechanical re-quotes hold (10:12 in full; 21:11 → 21:10); the sentences around them mended so the full verses read as sentences.
summary_md: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 1:6). These are the Watchers — the *sons of Elohim (God)* of Genesis 6 who *saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives,* and *there were giants in the earth in those days* (Genesis 6:1-4). They left their own habitation and broke the bound order, and the library tells in full what Jude names in brief. Yahuah (God) commanded, *Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness... on the day of the great judgement he shall be cast into the fire* (1 Enoch 10:4-6). For Semjaza and his company the order was the same, with the term of it fixed: *And when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated.* (1 Enoch 10:12), and then to be *led off to the abyss of fire... the prison in which they shall be confined for ever* (1 Enoch 10:13). Enoch was sent to pronounce the sentence already gone forth: *Azâzêl, thou shalt have no peace: a severe sentence has gone forth against thee to put thee in bonds* (1 Enoch 13:1); and on his journeys he was shown the place itself: *And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’* (1 Enoch 21:10). Jubilees says the same: the angels are *bound in the depths of the earth... for ever, until the day of the great condemnation* (Jubilees 5:6,10). This is the third canonical pass over the Watchers — Peter wrote it twice: the *spirits in prison... in the days of Noah* to whom the Formed Son preached (1 Peter 3:19-20), and *the angels that sinned... delivered into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). Jude, Peter, Genesis, 1 Enoch, and Jubilees hold one settled witness: the everlasting chains, the darkness, the judgment of the great day. The faith once delivered names the Watchers as Jude names them; the antinomians who left the faith are warned by the angels who left their estate.

title: Leaves without fruit — the fig tree, the unfruitful branches of Wisdom and Sirach, and the flock torn when its shepherds fall away
note: Degraded prose rewritten from scratch; the invented 89:35 quote replaced with the live 89:54-55; Wisdom 4:4-5 and Sirach 23:25 quotes kept; Matthew 21:19 from the index.
summary_md: *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on you henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). The tree had the look of a tree in season and nothing under the leaves, and the King's hand on it was a prophet's act against a leadership that had the same look. The prophets had used the fig that way for a long time, Hosea and Jeremiah and Joel and Micah all going to the tree for fruit and finding none. The Wisdom of Solomon says what becomes of such a tree: *for though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out* (the Wisdom of Solomon 4:4), and *the imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yes, meet for nothing* (the Wisdom of Solomon 4:5). Sirach says the same of the line that has no root: *her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit* (Ecclesiasticus 23:25). The Animal Apocalypse shows what it costs the flock when the ones set over it forsake the house: *And after that I saw that when they forsook the house of Yahuah (Lord) and His tower they fell away entirely, and their eyes were blinded; and I saw Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep how He wrought much slaughter amongst them in their herds until those sheep invited that slaughter and betrayed His place. And He gave them over into the hands of the lions and tigers, and wolves and hyenas, and into the hand of the foxes, and to all the wild beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear in pieces those sheep.* (1 Enoch 89:54-55). The curse on the tree is not a curse on Yashar'el (Israel). It falls on the leaders with leaves and no fruit, the same men the woes of Matthew 23 are spoken to, the shepherds Ezekiel 34 and Jeremiah 23 said fed themselves and scattered the sheep. Leaves without fruit leave a flock without a shepherd, and the good shepherd came for the flock those shepherds scattered.

title: The light of the elect and the throne of glory
note: Citation-only gloss rewritten with 38:2, 38:4 and 58:3 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew 5:14 and 5:16 from the index.
summary_md: *You are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.* (Matthew 5:14). *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 5:16). He does not tell them to become the light. He tells them what they are, and the Parables of Enoch say where that light comes from and whose face it rests on: *And the righteous shall be in the light of the sun, And the elect in the light of eternal life: The days of their life shall be unending, And the days of the holy without number.* (1 Enoch 58:3). The first Parable opens with the same light appearing on the same people, and the powerful of the earth unable to look at it: *From that time those that possess the earth shall no longer be powerful and exalted: And they shall not be able to behold the face of the holy, For Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits has caused His light to appear On the face of the holy, righteous, and elect.* (1 Enoch 38:4). And it is the Righteous One's own appearing that lights them: *And when the Righteous One shall appear before the eyes of the righteous, Whose elect works hang upon Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And light shall appear to the righteous and the elect who dwell on the earth, Where then will be the dwelling of the sinners, And where the resting-place of those who have denied Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits? It had been good for them if they had not been born.* (1 Enoch 38:2). The disciples are the light because they are the elect, and the light is his. A city on a hill in this age is the first showing of the face of the holy that the mighty will not be able to look upon in that day, and the good works that make men glorify the Father are the elect works that hang upon him.

title: Gabriel, that stand in the presence — the named angel of the presence in 1 Enoch
note: Citation-only; 40:2 and 40:9 now quoted in full from the live text; Luke 1:19 from the index.
summary_md: *And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of Elohim (God); and am sent to speak unto you, and to shew you these glad tidings.* (Luke 1:19). He gives the priest his name and his post, and both were already written. Enoch saw the post: *And on the four sides of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those that sleep not, and I learnt their names: for the angel that went with me made known to me their names, and showed me all the hidden things.* (1 Enoch 40:2). And he was given the names: *And he said to me: ‘This first is Michael, the merciful and long- suffering: and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.’* (1 Enoch 40:9). Gabriel is the third of the four who stand on the four sides of the throne, and the gospel sends that same angel from that same place to the altar of incense. The roster even follows into the next chapter, where Anna is *the daughter of Phanuel* (Luke 2:36). The angel who stands in the presence is not a New Testament invention. Luke names the one Enoch had already seen standing there.

title: Satan fallen as lightning — the watcher-fall in 1 Enoch and Wisdom of Solomon
note: Quotes stand; prose plained (no 'wisdom-stream', 'administration', 'inaugurated'); the internal note at the end removed.
summary_md: *And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.* (Luke 10:18). *Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy* (Luke 10:19). Seven words name a fall the Hebrew library had told at length. The King says it as the seventy come back glad that *even the devils are subject unto us through thy name* (Luke 10:17), town by town taking ground from the unclean spirits whose master he had watched come down. Enoch tells how the coming down began, by their own oath: *And they were in all two hundred; who descended in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon, and they called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn and bound themselves by mutual imprecations upon it.* (1 Enoch 6:6). And he shows where a fallen star ends up: *And I saw one of those four who had come forth first, and he seized that first star which had fallen from the heaven, and bound it hand and foot and cast it into an abyss: now that abyss was narrow and deep, and horrible and dark.* (1 Enoch 88:1). The Wisdom of Solomon names what the fall brought with it: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (the Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). The enemy the seventy are given power to tread on is the devil whose envy was the door death came through, and the spirits they drive out are what is left loose of the host that came down on Hermon. The King names the fall in seven words and sends his men out against what it left behind.
